title: Elliptic Curve Cryptosystems

title: PRIMES is in P
authors: Manindra Agrawal, Neeraj Kayal, Nitin Saxena

title: On Artin's conjecture
plainSummary: Hooley proves Artin's conjecture that a fixed integer is a primitive root modulo infinitely many primes, assuming the generalized Riemann hypothesis for Dedekind zeta functions of Kummer number fields.

plainFallbackNote: No unconditional proof of Artin's primitive root conjecture is known; Hooley's result is purely conditional on the number-field GRH.

title: Explicit bounds for primality testing and related problems

plainFallbackNote: Unconditional primality testing exists via other methods (e.g., later AKS), but this paper proves no unconditional version of its GRH-conditional bound.

plainSummary: The paper gives a quantum algorithm for decomposing finite abelian groups, enabling the abelian hidden subgroup algorithm and, conditionally, fast class number computation.
plainImpactUpgrade: A machine-checked proof of RH and Dirichlet GRH does not settle this, since the class number application needs GRH for quadratic number field zeta functions.
plainFallbackNote: No unconditional efficient algorithm for class number computation is known or provided in this paper.
extractedQuote: assuming the generalized Riemann Hypothesis we can apply the algorithm in this paper and efficiently find class numbers (a problem known to be at least as hard as factoring)

title: The Torelli locus and special subvarieties
plainSummary: This survey discusses special Shimura subvarieties inside the Torelli locus and the André–Oort conjecture, whose conditional proof assumes the Riemann hypothesis for CM fields.
plainImpactUpgrade: A machine-checked proof of classical RH and Dirichlet GRH does not settle the CM-field GRH needed here, so the paper's conditional results remain open.
plainFallbackNote: Some special cases of the André–Oort conjecture, notably André's theorem, are already known unconditionally, as the survey notes.
extractedQuote: Klingler and Yafaev, using the work of Ullmo and Yafaev, have announced a proof of the André-Oort conjecture, assuming the Generalized Riemann hypothesis (GRH) for CM fields.

title: Rational 6-Cycles Under Iteration of Quadratic Polynomials
plainSummary: Assuming the Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer Conjecture for a specific abelian variety, no rational numbers give exact period six under iterating a quadratic polynomial.
plainImpactUpgrade: A machine-checked proof of RH and Dirichlet GRH changes nothing here, since the paper's theorem rests on the Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer Conjecture, not on RH or GRH.
plainFallbackNote: No unconditional substitute is proved here; GRH appears only in remarks noting that class-group computations for a degree-119 field remain infeasible even assuming it.
extractedQuote: We present a proof, which is conditional on the Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer Conjecture for a specific abelian variety, that there do not exist rational numbers x and c such that x has exact period N = 6 under the iteration x ↦ x2 + c.

title: A strengthening of the Nyman-Beurling criterion for the Riemann Hypothesis
plainSummary: The paper proves that the Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to density of a smaller family of fractional-part functions in a Hilbert space.
plainImpactUpgrade: A machine-checked proof of RH would make the paper's equivalence unconditional, confirming density of the natural Beurling subspace.
plainFallbackNote: The paper proves unconditionally that the smoothed approximants converge to the characteristic function, giving an unconditional half of the argument.

title: Computing discrete logarithms in high-genus hyperelliptic Jacobians in provably subexponential time
plainSummary: The paper gives a provably subexponential algorithm for computing discrete logarithms in Jacobians of high-genus hyperelliptic curves over finite fields.

authors: Andrea Basso, Giulio Codogni, Deirdre Connolly et al.

plainSummary: The paper develops inversion techniques for Dirichlet series and derives asymptotic estimates for prime counting, prime gaps, and divisor functions, with refined error terms under the Riemann Hypothesis.
plainImpactUpgrade: A machine-checked proof of RH would upgrade the paper's conditional error terms, such as the refined prime characteristic and prime-pair approximations, to unconditional theorems.
plainFallbackNote: The paper also proves unconditional average-order asymptotics for these prime-related functions, which remain valid without RH.
extractedQuote: This paper also analyzes prime gaps, prime k-tuples, and divisor functions, providing asymptotic results and error estimates under the Riemann Hypothesis.

title: Euler Product Asymptotics for L-functions of Elliptic Curves
plainSummary: Assuming the Riemann Hypothesis for an elliptic curve's L-function, the paper shows point-count Euler products grow like a power of log outside a small exceptional set.
plainImpactUpgrade: A machine-checked proof of classical RH and Dirichlet GRH does not supply the needed RH for elliptic-curve L-functions, so the paper's conditional theorems remain open.
plainFallbackNote: No unconditional version of the Euler product asymptotic is proved here; the results all assume the elliptic-curve Riemann Hypothesis.

title: The 1 -Level Density for Zeros of Hecke L -Functions of Imaginary Quadratic Number Fields of Class Number 1
plainSummary: Computes the average spacing distribution of zeros of Hecke L-functions of imaginary quadratic fields, unconditionally for restricted test functions and conditionally for lower-order terms.
plainImpactUpgrade: A machine-checked proof of RH and Dirichlet GRH does not settle this paper's conditional result, since it concerns Hecke L-functions of number fields and additionally assumes the unproved Ratios Conjecture.
plainFallbackNote: The paper proves an unconditional 1-level density asymptotic for test functions whose Fourier transforms are supported in (-1, 1), agreeing with the conjectural prediction.

title: Real moments of the logarithmic derivative of characteristic polynomials in random matrix ensembles
plainSummary: The paper proves unconditional asymptotics for real moments of logarithmic derivatives of characteristic polynomials in classical random matrix ensembles.
plainImpactUpgrade: A machine-checked proof of RH and Dirichlet GRH leaves this paper unchanged, since its random-matrix moment theorems are already unconditional.
plainFallbackNote: The main asymptotics are proved unconditionally; RH appears only in motivating discussion of zeta moment conjectures.

title: Spectral Geometry of the Primes
plainSummary: The paper builds self-adjoint operators on the primes and shows unconditionally that their heat trace yields an effective spectral dimension of one half.
plainImpactUpgrade: A machine-checked proof of RH would only strengthen the paper's speculative analogy between its spectra and zeta zeros, leaving its unconditional results unchanged.
plainFallbackNote: The main spectral dimension result is proved from first principles without assuming the Riemann Hypothesis, so no conditional fallback is needed.
extractedQuote: Our principal analytic result is derived from first principles and does not rely on the Riemann Hypothesis.

title: Primes in almost all short intervals II
shortLabel: primes in almost all short intervals
plainSummary: The paper proves unconditionally that intervals of length about n to the 1/22 plus epsilon before n contain primes for almost all n, improving the previous exponent.
plainImpactUpgrade: A machine-checked proof of RH would give primes in every interval of length n theta for theta above one half, far stronger than this almost-all result, so this paper remains unchanged.
plainFallbackNote: The theorem itself is unconditional, proved by sieve methods and zero-density estimates with no reliance on RH or GRH.

title: Integer moments of the derivatives of the Riemann zeta function
plainSummary: The paper formulates conjectures, via random matrix theory and the Ratios Conjecture, for asymptotic moments of derivatives of the zeta function at its zeros.
plainImpactUpgrade: A machine-checked RH proof would not settle these conjectures, since they rest on additional heuristic recipes beyond RH itself.
plainFallbackNote: Earlier special cases, such as sums of zeta derivatives at zeros, are already proved unconditionally or under RH in prior work.

plainSummary: The paper proves that the generalized Fermat equation x^13 + y^13 = z^n has only trivial solutions for n=5 unconditionally and for n=7 assuming a generalized Riemann hypothesis.
plainImpactUpgrade: A machine-checked proof of RH and Dirichlet GRH would not settle the n=7 case, since the paper needs GRH for class groups of a number field, which remains open.
plainFallbackNote: The n=5 case and the divisibility condition 13|c are proved unconditionally, so partial unconditional results already exist.
extractedQuote: Let $p \in \{5,7\}$ and assume GRH if $p=7$. Then the only solutions to the generalized Fermat equation ... are the trivial solutions

title: Equidistribution of Kloosterman Sums Over Function Fields
authors: Lei Fu, Yuk-Kam Lau, Wen-Ching Winnie Li et al.
plainSummary: The paper proves Sato–Tate equidistribution of Kloosterman sums over function fields, with explicit error terms, as places vary in arithmetic progressions or short intervals.
plainImpactUpgrade: A machine-checked proof of the classical and Dirichlet Riemann hypotheses changes nothing here, since the results rely only on Weil's already-proved Riemann hypothesis for curves over finite fields.
plainFallbackNote: No conditional hypotheses are needed: the effective Chebotarev density theorem for function fields is proved unconditionally via Weil's theorem.
extractedQuote: A consequence of the Riemann Hypothesis for curves over finite fields is an effective version of the Chebotarev density theorem for function fields, which can be regarded as an analogue of the work of Lagarias and Odlyzko for number fields.

title: The Generalized Fermat Equation $x^2 + y^3 = z^{25}$
plainSummary: The paper reduces the generalized Fermat equation x^2 + y^3 = z^25 to five specific degree-ten equations over a sextic number field, leaving those five unresolved.
plainImpactUpgrade: A machine-checked proof of RH and Dirichlet GRH would not finish the argument, since the remaining gap is class-group computations in degree-60 fields that GRH already cannot make feasible.
plainFallbackNote: No unconditional resolution of the five remaining equations is achieved; the paper's main theorem is conditional on their expected solution sets, not on GRH.
extractedQuote: Unfortunately, we are left with five~equations that are out of reach of current methods and computational resources even when assuming~GRH.

title: Irreducibility of Random Polynomials of ℤ[X]

plainImpactUpgrade: A machine-checked RH and Dirichlet GRH proof changes nothing here, since the paper's main theorems already remove GRH and Artin holomorphy assumptions.
plainFallbackNote: The paper itself is unconditional, replacing GRH with large sieve estimates for Artin L-functions and an unconditional Chebotarev theorem.
extractedQuote: Our method removes the assumptions of GRH and Artin's holomorphy conjecture from an argument of Duke (2003) by following the strategy of Lemke Oliver, Thorner, and Zaman (2024) on the existence of extremal class numbers for number fields of arbitrary degree.

title: Orders in the Euclidean Court
authors: Carlo Francisco Adajar, Kevin J. McGown, Paul Pollack et al.
plainSummary: The paper proves only finitely many quadratic orders are generalized Euclidean, and finitely many pure orders of each degree, with the odd-degree case conditional on GRH.
plainImpactUpgrade: A machine-checked GRH for Dirichlet L-functions alone does not settle the odd-degree case, since the proof invokes GRH-conditional Chebotarev for Kummer number-field extensions.
plainFallbackNote: For even degree the finiteness result is proved unconditionally, so half of the main theorem needs no GRH.
extractedQuote: Additionally, assuming GRH, we show that for each fixed $d > 1$ there are only finitely many integers $m$ for which $T^d-m$ is irreducible over $\mathbb{Q}$ and $\mathbb{Z}[m^{1/d}] = \mathbb{Z}[T]/(T^d-m)$ is generalized Euclidean.

title: $6$ powers of $2$ in the Linnik--Goldbach problem
plainSummary: The paper proves every large even integer is a sum of two primes plus at most six powers of two unconditionally, and at most five assuming the generalized Riemann hypothesis.
plainImpactUpgrade: A machine-checked proof of Dirichlet GRH would make the five-powers theorem unconditional, while the six-powers result already stands unconditionally.
plainFallbackNote: An unconditional six-powers theorem is proved in this same paper, so the GRH result has a direct unconditional fallback one power weaker.
extractedQuote: We prove that $6$ powers of $2$ suffice unconditionally and that $5$ suffice under the GRH, improving previous works.

title: Fields with no everywhere good abelian varieties
plainSummary: Assuming the generalized Riemann hypothesis for number fields, the authors find thousands of number fields of degree up to 16 over which no abelian variety has good reduction everywhere.
plainImpactUpgrade: A machine-checked proof of RH and Dirichlet GRH does not settle this paper, which needs GRH for Dedekind zeta functions of general number fields.
plainFallbackNote: No unconditional substitute is proved here; the unconditional Fontaine–Abrashkin–Schoof criteria cover only a small known list of fields.

plainFallbackNote: The paper unconditionally proves that every Euclidean system of ray classes generates the corresponding ray class group, but the GRH existence criterion has no unconditional substitute here.

plainSummary: The paper links local vanishing densities to growth of divisor moments, recovering unconditional polynomial-value estimates and, assuming GRH, proving divisor moment bounds for polynomials in Fourier coefficients of modular eigenforms.
plainImpactUpgrade: A machine-checked proof of RH and Dirichlet GRH would not remove the paper's reliance on GRH for Dedekind zeta functions and symmetric power L-functions, so its modular-form results remain open.

title: Improved bounds for Szpiro's conjecture
plainSummary: The paper unconditionally improves bounds for Szpiro's conjecture for elliptic curves over the rationals, matching a bound previously known only conditionally.
plainImpactUpgrade: A machine-checked Riemann Hypothesis and Dirichlet GRH change nothing here, since the previously conditional bound is now proved unconditionally.

title: Improved average and almost-all bounds for $G(n)$
plainSummary: The paper proves unconditional average and almost-all bounds for the least integer whose coprime residues generate the multiplicative group modulo n.
plainImpactUpgrade: A machine-checked proof of RH and Dirichlet GRH would only confirm the classical pointwise bound already matched here unconditionally for almost all n.

plainSummary: The paper improves error terms for counting cubic number fields and proves one-level density and non-vanishing results for their Artin L-functions, conditionally on the Riemann hypothesis for Dedekind zeta functions.

authors: Sung Min Lee, Jacob Mayle, Rakvi

plainSummary: The paper gives an asymptotic for a Möbius series over integers with prescribed smallest prime factor, and shows under GRH that most reduced residue classes give negative constants.

authors: Zikang Dong, Ruihua Wang, Weijia Wang et al.

plainSummary: The paper studies the power and limits of dynamic-programming circuits over min-plus semirings, defining a verifiable-certificate class and proving separation and simulation dichotomies.
